boundary_evidence: tu_map CANNOT segment this module: tools/tu_map.py emits `main` as ONE unit covering 0x20049f0..0x20707a4 with 2984 functions and ~70 class labels, and lists the module under `under-segmented (TU count is a lower bound)`. There is therefore no `tubuild.py create` candidate id for Scene and NO tu_map boundary behind any of the readings below -- all of them were established by hand from the cartridge.
contiguous linker run: 0x0202e140..0x0202ec9c, 21 function(s), gapless in config/arm9/delinks.txt (each entry's end is the next entry's start, all 21 marked `complete`).

neighbours differ on both sides: func_0202e118 (0x0202e118..0x0202e140) ends exactly where the run begins and the Stage_Spawn allocation factory sits below it; func_0202ec9c begins exactly where the run ends. Neither is a Scene member and neither is called from one.

TWO FOREIGN-NAMED FUNCTIONS SIT INSIDE THE SPAN and are admitted deliberately: _ZN5Stage12SetVramBanksEv (0x0202e73c) and _ZN2GX15DisableAllBanksEv (0x0202e78c) lie between _ZN8dScene_c20Initialise3dGraphicsEv (0x0202e6c8) and _ZN8dScene_c22ResetHardwareRegistersEv (0x0202e7d4). An object's contribution to a section is a single contiguous interval, so if those two Scene functions share an object then so do the two between them. The data attribution below is what establishes that they do.

STATIC-DATA ATTRIBUTION, which is the decisive reading. This TU's statics form one unbroken .data block ending in the vtable it is the key-function TU for: data_02092660 (u8) / data_02092664 (u16) / data_02092668 (Matrix2x2, 0x10 bytes, ending 0x02092678) / _ZTV8dScene_c's Itanium preamble at 0x02092678 / _ZTV8dScene_c at 0x02092680, 18 slots, ending 0x020926c8 where the next symbol data_020926c8 begins. From config/arm9/relocs.txt those three statics are referenced ONLY from inside this span, and from BOTH SIDES of the foreign pair: data_02092660 <- 0x0202e2f0, 0x0202e344, 0x0202e5e8; data_02092664 <- 0x0202e2f4, 0x0202e340, 0x0202e390, 0x0202e5c4 (all BELOW the pair); data_02092668 <- 0x0202ebe4, which is inside ResetHardwareRegisters, ABOVE the pair. Object k's contribution to EVERY section precedes object k+1's, in ascending disjoint intervals, so one object owns 0x02092660..0x020926c8; both text sub-runs reach into it; therefore both sub-runs are that one object, and the pair between them is inside it.

the source order the reverse-emission rule implies is a coherent file: reversing the ROM address order yields BeforeInitResources then AfterInitResources, then the Cleanup pair, then Behavior, then Render -- each Before immediately before its After, the four groups in ActorBase's own declaration order, destructor last. Corroboration, not proof.

THE FOUR GraphCallbacks ARE EXCLUDED, on evidence, not omission. _ZN8dGraph_c10callback_c14GraphCallback0Ev..3Ev are at 0x02018ea0..0x02018ec0, 0x152a0 bytes below this run. The same single-contiguous-interval rule the admission of the foreign pair rests on excludes them outright: no object can contribute .text at both 0x02018ea0 and 0x0202e140 with ~86 KB of other objects' code in between. Three further readings agree: (a) their neighbours are func_02018e68, an OS_SleepThread wrapper, and func_02018ec0, a fader slot-2 dispatch -- a system/graphics grab-bag, not a scene class; (b) the pointer tables holding them, 0x0208ee14..0x0208ee20, are ~0x3800 bytes below this TU's .data block and on the far side of _ZTV7dBase_c (0x0208e4b8), i.e. in a much earlier object's data contribution; (c) their own address order reverses to GraphCallback0,1,2,3, so they ARE consecutive definitions in one source file -- just not this one. Which TU is theirs was not established.

notes: HAND-ASSEMBLED. `tubuild.py create` has no candidate for this TU (see boundary_evidence item 1) and would refuse these sources anyway, several being extern "C"-wrapped. Written against notes/tu-reconstruction-pilot-report.md and src_tu/actors/daObjKm2_Ami_Bou_c.cpp; the manifest entry itself is built by tubuild.build_manifest_entry so the schema stays the tool's own.

The two functions at 0x0202e73c and 0x0202e78c carry other classes' names (Stage::SetVramBanks, GX::DisableAllBanks) and are admitted on the data-attribution reading in boundary_evidence, not on their names. Names in this tree are project coinages; the ROM's RTTI carries class names only.

ZERO UNLICENSED .text, AND THAT TOOK REMOVING A SCAFFOLD RATHER THAN ADDING ONE. ~Scene() is defined INLINE in include/Scene.h, and src/_ZN8dScene_cD1Ev.cpp / src/_ZN8dScene_cD0Ev.cpp each carry a never-called forcing function because a TU that merely includes the header emits no out-of-line copy. This TU needs no such thing: it defines Scene's key function (BeforeInitResources, the first non-inline virtual), so it emits _ZTV8dScene_c, whose slots 16/17 ARE D1/D0, and taking their addresses for the table forces both out-of-line copies. MEASURED both ways -- `tubuild.py compile` reports D1 at section[16] size 0x30 and D0 at section[18] size 0x44 with the scaffold and without it; dropping it took unlicensed function symbols 1 -> 0. It was worth dropping and not merely tidy: a 0x38-byte STB_GLOBAL .text that no config/arm9/symbols.txt entry names, sitting inside the licensed span, displaces every byte after it under rombuild's -nodead link (measured on arm9/Actor: 506 bytes differ and 15/106 modules exact with a scaffold, IDENTICAL and 106/106 without).

UNLICENSED .data, 7 symbols, ALL EXPECTED AND NONE VERIFIED. Defining the key function emits _ZTV8dScene_c (0x50, STB_GLOBAL) plus six STB_LOPROC RTTI records for Scene and its bases. _ZTV8dScene_c is ROM-resident at 0x02092678..0x020926c8 -- inside the 0x02092660..0x020926c8 block boundary_evidence establishes this TU owns -- so it is licensable in principle, but it is deliberately NOT listed under `data` here: every one of its 20 words is a relocation, `verify` does not compare data at all, and listing it would only stop the tool reporting it while proving nothing. That is the `data-verified` rung and this round did not attempt it. Note also the convention clash the pilot hit in the text direction: mwcc's `_ZTV8dScene_c` names the vtable OBJECT at 0x02092678 while config/arm9/symbols.txt names the SLOT ARRAY at 0x02092680, eight bytes apart.

boundary_confidence 'high' came out of tubuild.tu_confidence's DEGENERATE path -- with a single synthetic unit it has no neighbouring unit to score against and returns 'high' merely because the unit carries a class label. It is NOT a tu_map boundary_confidence reading, because tu_map has no boundary here at all. The real basis for trusting this cut is the boundary_evidence list, item 5 in particular.

LADDER REACHED: status text-verified on the whole-range axis (whole-range linking is walled -- see verification.linkcheck.whyWholeRangeCannotPassYet), and partial-link-verified on the orthogonal partial-isolation axis, where the TU range 0x0202e140..0x0202ec9c comes out IDENTICAL (2908 bytes, 0 differing), module fidelity is 106/106 exact at 100.000000%, dsd check modules --fail PASSes, and the full ROM builds bit-identical to the baseline control.

GENERAL FINDING, worth lifting out of this entry: a key-function TU emits _ZTS records whose bytes are the CLASS NAME STRING, so while the tree's class names are coinages those records can never be attributed to any ROM address -- the ROM holds b'8dScene_c\x00' where this TU emits b'8dScene_c\x00'. That makes whole-range link-verified unreachable for every coinage-named key-function TU, independently of the tubuild.splice_tu_entry .data-claim gap. See verification.linkcheck.whyWholeRangeCannotPassYet blockers A and B.

Errors caused tool to abort.
whyWholeRangeCannotPassYet: THE KEY-FUNCTION LINK WALL, measured rather than predicted. This TU defines Scene's key function, so it emits _ZTV8dScene_c STB_GLOBAL; dsd's gap object supplies the same symbol from ROM data at arm9:0x02092680, and mwldarm aborts: 'Multiply-defined: "virtual table for Scene" in Scene.o / Previously defined in _dsd_gap@main_44.o'. The licensing audit predicted it (1 COLLIDES-GAP) and the link was run anyway so the verdict was measured.

BLOCKER A -- TOOLING, in principle fixable. To stop the gap object claiming the vtable the TU would have to OWN the .data it lands in. tubuild.splice_tu_entry cannot express that: it hardcodes a single `.text start:.. end:..` line per spliced entry with no path for any other section. The range is already known from boundary_evidence (0x02092660..0x020926c8, the vtable object occupying 0x02092678..0x020926c8), so the claim is knowable; writing it is not currently possible. _ZTV8dScene_c's own 20 words are plausible content -- every slot points at a real ROM function -- so this blocker is about plumbing, not about the bytes.

BLOCKER B -- NAMING, AND IT IS NOT FIXABLE BY ATTRIBUTION AT ALL. This is the important one and it generalises past this TU. The object emits six STB_LOPROC RTTI records that the audit calls HOMELESS -- _ZTI/_ZTS for Scene, ActorDerived and ActorBase -- and no symbols.txt anywhere names them (verified: zero hits across every config/**/symbols.txt; the only matches in config/ are inside this manifest file itself). The reason is that the type-name STRINGS a C++ compiler bakes into _ZTS are the CLASS NAMES, and this tree's names are coinages while the cartridge holds Nintendo's. Measured side by side:

b'8dScene_c\x00' is 7 bytes and b'8dScene_c\x00' is 10, and they are different bytes, so there is no address in the cartridge these three _ZTS records could be attributed to -- their content is not in the ROM and never will be. Since rombuild links -nodead, nothing drops them either, and they would displace bytes inside the module.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WORKSTREAM, stated as a general rule because it is one: NO key-function TU can reach whole-range link-verified while its class name is a project coinage. The vtable is a plumbing problem; the type strings are not. The only fix is renaming the class to the ROM's own name (Scene -> dScene_c, ActorDerived -> dBase_c, ActorBase -> fBase_c, per include/Scene.h reading 4), which is a separate tree-wide change and was not attempted here.

WHY --partial IS UNAFFECTED: objisolate.derive drops exactly this material per function, which is why the partial route reproduces the module and the ROM byte-for-byte while the whole-range splice cannot. Neither blocker is a source change to this file, and the text-only result stands regardless -- a linkcheck failure says nothing about it.
